references.text: The Lord predicts that He will harden Pharaoh's heart, so that he will not let the people go.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he refused to let the Israelites go, just as the Lord had said.
The Lord warns that all the firstborn in Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh to the firstborn of the slave woman.
Describes the actual execution of the tenth plague where the Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt.
The Lord commands that all firstborn, both humans and animals, be consecrated to Him.
Describes the command to give to the Lord everything that opens the womb, and that firstborn sons must be redeemed.
Repeats the command that all firstborn belong to the Lord, and that firstborn sons must be redeemed.
Explains that all firstborn belong to the Lord from the day He struck down all the firstborn in Egypt.
Confirms that all firstborn in Israel, both humans and animals, belong to the Lord after the plague in Egypt.
Describes the rules for redemption money for firstborn humans who must be redeemed.
Cites the law that every male firstborn shall be called holy to the Lord.
Refers to the Passover celebration and the application of blood that protected the Israelite firstborn when the destroyer passed through Egypt.
The actual execution of the plague that establishes the commandment of redemption.
Historical confirmation of the plague as the basis for the law concerning the firstborn.
